title: Sessions
summary: Chapter 6 explains how Vim sessions record the current workspace, including buffers, window layout, tab pages, and cursor position, so that state can be restored after restarting Vim. It demonstrates saving with :mksession!, reloading with vim -S or :source, and automating the process with Tim Pope's Obsession plugin. It then covers persistent undo through the 'undofile' and 'undodir' options, including an autocommand that disables undo files for temporary files, and shows how Neovim terminal buffers can be renamed so their processes are restarted when a session is restored.

concepts.name: Session as a workspace snapshot
concepts.evidence: With Vim’s sessions feature you can record the state of your workspace, enabling you to restore that state later on.

concepts.name: A session can represent a project
concepts.evidence: When used this way, a Vim session represents a project.

concepts.name: Default Session.vim file
concepts.evidence: Vim records the current session in a Session.vim file in the current working directory.

concepts.name: Obsession autocommands on VimLeavePre and BufEnter
concepts.evidence: This sets up an autocommand so that the :mksession! command is triggered whenever the VimLeavePre or BufEnter events fire (see Tip 26, Using Autocommands to Respond to Events).

concepts.name: 'sessionoptions' controls what a session records
concepts.evidence: The ‘sessionoptions’ option specifies what will be recorded when you save a session (:help ’sessionoptions’).

concepts.name: Buffer names are preserved, buffer numbers are not
concepts.evidence: Buffer names are preserved, but buffer numbers are not.

concepts.name: Neovim shada file for shared state
concepts.evidence: In Neovim, this is called the shada file, which is short for shared data (:h shada-file).

concepts.name: Persistent undo with 'undofile'
concepts.evidence: By enabling Vim’s ‘undofile’ option, you can make undo history persist between editing sessions.

concepts.name: 'undodir' designated undo directory
concepts.evidence: To avoid this, use the ‘undodir’ option to specify a directory where your undo files will be saved.

concepts.name: Local noundofile autocommand for temporary files
concepts.evidence: To avoid this situation, use an autocommand to disable ‘undofile’ locally for files that match a particular pattern.

concepts.name: Terminal buffer name format term://{cwd}//{pid}:{cmd}
concepts.evidence: These can be generalized as term://{cwd}//{pid}:{cmd}.

concepts.name: Renaming terminal buffers with :file {name}
concepts.evidence: You can use the :file {name} command to rename your terminal buffers (:help :file_f).
